stimulus.body: The log warns that attendre means to wait, not to attend.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Which pairs belong to one verb family
questions.learningObjective: Identify pairs in one verb family
questions.stem: Entry 0051 in the train dispatcher's log asks which set belongs to one verb family.
questions.explanation: Aller and its forms belong to one verb family. The tempting wrong idea mixes aller with etre, avoir, or faire forms.
questions.hint: Keep one verb's forms together.

questions.subject: FRENCH
questions.topic: Teaching a routine against false friends
questions.learningObjective: Teach a routine against false friends

stimulus.body: The log warns that attendre means to wait, not to attend.

questions.stem: Entry 0052 in the train dispatcher's log asks which statement teaches a routine against false friends.

options.text: attendre means to attend a meeting
attendre means to wait, not to attend
assister means to help, not attend
demander means to demand, not ask

questions.explanation: Attendre means to wait, not to attend, which counters the false friend. The tempting wrong idea repeats the false translation.
questions.hint: Think of the English trap.

options.text: je vous en prie for you're welcome

questions.explanation: Je vous en prie is the polite service counter phrase. The tempting wrong idea uses informal or third person pronouns.
questions.hint: Think of polite customer service.

questions.topic: A courier note written in shorthand
questions.learningObjective: Decode a courier note shorthand
questions.stem: Entry 0054 in the train dispatcher's log asks what RAS means in a courier note.

answer.exemplar: In a courier note, RAS means rien a signaler, indicating nothing to report.

questions.explanation: RAS means rien a signaler in a courier note. The tempting wrong idea reads it as a meeting or reply code.
questions.hint: Think of nothing to report.
